newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Investment fund focuses on rural Australia.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Investment fund focuses on rural Australia.

text.p: Prudential Corp Australia Ltd said on Wednesday it hoped to raise at least A$50 million via a new rural investment fund targeting the livestock and wool trade.

The unlisted unit trust, called the Rural Investment Fund, will allow investors to "buy a piece of the farm," and provide exposure to the export markets of Asia for live Australian cattle, which has risen on average by 45 percent since 1991, Ian Horton, managing director of Prudential Portfolio Managers Australia, told reporters.

Prudential also plans to invest in Australian wool production, capitalising on what it sees as expectations that the long-suffering wool market is poised for recovery, with demand outstripping supply in the next two years, Horton said.
The fund already owns three cattle properties located in New South Wales and Queensland states valued at about A$45 million and plans to buy more, Horton said.
Australia's rural sector was becoming increasingly institutionalised as exports of rural commodities increases, Allan Hayes, manager of the Prudential Pastoral Co Ltd said.
"Right now there is no access for collective capital to get to the bush," Hayes said.
Horton said he expects rural investments to perform in line with other "major asset classes."
The non-redemption clause contained in the fund meant that short-term investors would probably shy away from the fund, despite the cyclical nature of rural commodities, Horton said.
The fund is aimed at domestic institutional and other large investors initially, although Prudential has not ruled out interest among international investors, Horton said.
Prudential will be looking at both corporate and private rural holdings, but has no interest in integrating operations to include downstream slaughtering ad processing, Hayes said.
A promotional film accompanying the launch of the fund highlights the "top end" of Australia for potential investment given the proximity to Asia.
